api_traffic.description: Lists the API endpoints the open Teams tab has called since the browser started: method, host, path, status, which headers were sent (names only, never values) and the auth scheme. Used to find out which API Teams uses for a feature: click through it in Teams first.

filter.description: Only requests whose host or path contains this text

clear.description: Clear the recorded traffic after returning it

find_people.description: Looks people up by name or email in your organization (and people you work with), as in Teams' people picker: name, email, job title, department, office.

get_meeting.description: One meeting with the calls held in it, newest first (a recurring meeting has one per occurrence): when it started and ended, who joined, the recording's link, and whether there is a transcript.

meeting.description: Which meeting: its chat id from list_meetings (19:meeting_…) or its title. A title must match exactly one meeting chat.

get_version.description: Shows the mcp-teams server version, the browser extension version, and whether Teams is reachable (which of its services have a session).

list_chats.description: Lists your chats (1:1, group and meeting chats), most recent first, with their title (or the other members' names), the last message and whether it is unread. Returns ids for read_messages and send_message.

query.description: Only chats whose title or a member's name contains these words

list_meetings.description: Lists your Teams meetings (each scheduled meeting or recurring series has a meeting chat), most recent activity first: subject, scheduled time (for a series, its first occurrence), organizer, whether a transcript exists, and whether another organization hosted it (`external`: its chat and recordings are usually no longer readable afterwards). Use get_meeting for the calls held and who attended, read_transcript for what was said, read_messages for the meeting chat.

query.description: Only meetings whose subject or organizer contains these words

list_teams.description: Lists the teams you are a member of, each with its channels. Use 'Team/Channel' or a channel id as the conversation for read_messages and send_message.

include_ids.description: Also return team and channel ids (long; 'Team/Channel' names are enough to address channels)

read_messages.description: Reads the latest messages of a chat or channel, oldest first: sender, time, text (formatting removed), files shared and reactions. In channels, replies are nested under their post. To read further back, pass the returned olderBefore as `before`. With reply_to, reads one channel post's whole thread.

conversation.description: Which chat or channel: its id from list_chats/list_teams (19:…), 'Team/Channel' (e.g. 'Engineering/General'), a chat title, or a person's name for your 1:1 chat with them. A name must match exactly one conversation, otherwise the matches are listed.

limit.description: How many messages (channel: posts, each with its replies)

before.description: Only messages older than this time (ISO 8601, e.g. olderBefore from a previous call)

reply_to.description: Channel only: the id of a post, to read its thread

include_system.description: Also return events such as members added or calls started

max_length.description: Maximum length of each message's text

read_transcript.description: What was said in a meeting, from its Teams transcript: lines '[hh:mm:ss] Speaker: text', plus how long each speaker talked. Reads the latest call with a transcript unless `session` names another. Long transcripts are cut at max_length; pass the returned continueFrom as `from` to read on. Transcripts are stored in the organizer's OneDrive, so this may open OneDrive in a background tab.

meeting.description: Which meeting: its chat id from list_meetings (19:meeting_…) or its title. A title must match exactly one meeting chat.

session.description: Which call: its callId from get_meeting, or its start date/time prefix (e.g. '2026-10-06')

from.description: Start at this point of the meeting, 'hh:mm:ss' or 'mm:ss'

max_length.description: Most characters of transcript to return

reload_extension.description: Reloads the mcp-teams browser extension from disk, e.g. after an update changed it, and waits until it is connected again. Returns the extension version before and after. Refused while a send confirmation window is open.

search_messages.description: Searches all your Teams chats and channels with Microsoft Search, like the search box in Teams. Returns matching messages with their conversation id (for read_messages), sender, time and a highlighted excerpt.

query.description: Words to search for; Teams search syntax such as from:alice or "exact phrase" works too

search_transcripts.description: Finds what was said in meetings: the transcript lines containing all words of the query, each with the line before it, from the most recent meetings with a transcript (or one meeting). Then read_transcript with `from` reads around a match.

query.description: Words that must all appear in a line (case-insensitive)

meeting.description: Which meeting: its chat id from list_meetings (19:meeting_…) or its title. A title must match exactly one meeting chat.

meetings.description: How many of the most recent meetings with a transcript to search

send_message.description: Asks to post a message in an existing chat or channel (conversation), to reply to a channel post, or to start a chat with people (to): one person for a 1:1 chat, several for a group chat. If a chat with exactly those people already exists, the message goes there. The extension shows a confirmation window with the message, where it goes and who is in a new chat; nothing is posted, and no chat is created, unless the user clicks Send there. Returns whether it was sent. Plain text; line breaks are kept and links become clickable.

conversation.description: Which chat or channel: its id from list_chats/list_teams (19:…), 'Team/Channel' (e.g. 'Engineering/General'), a chat title, or a person's name for your 1:1 chat with them. A name must match exactly one conversation, otherwise the matches are listed.

to.description: Instead of conversation: the people to chat with, by name or email (e.g. ['김민준', 'ana@example.com']). Each must match exactly one person in your organization, otherwise the matches are listed.

title.description: With to (two or more people): a title for the new group chat

reply_to.description: Channel only: the id of the post to reply to (from read_messages). Without it, a new post is started.

subject.description: Channel only: a subject for a new post
